test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 23 Dec, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: What will be the amount after 1 year if a sum of ₹7,500 is invested at 8% compound interest per annum, compounded half-yearly?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For **half-yearly compounding**, Rate (R) becomes R/2 and Time (n) becomes 2n.

Effective Rate = 8% ÷ 2 = 4% per half-year.

Time periods = 1 year × 2 = 2 periods.

Effective % for 2 periods = 4 + 4 + (4 × 4)/100 = 8.16%.

Amount = 7500 × 108.16% = 75 × 108.16 = ₹8112.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹8112.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Principal (P)** = ₹7,500, **Rate (R)** = 8% p.a., **Time (n)** = 1 year.

**Formula Used:** Amount (A) = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/00e7fdd92b39669fb9a79b49f0d45608aa6c5c1cd45e8cdf99b0793dca22696f.png] 

⇒ For **compounded half-yearly**, New Rate (r) = 8%/2 = 4%.

⇒ New Time (T) = 1 × 2 = 2 periods.

⇒ A = 7500(1 + 4/100)²

⇒ A = 7500(1 + 1/25)²

⇒ A = 7500 × (26/25) × (26/25)

⇒ A = 12 × 26 × 26

⇒ A = 12 × 676 = 8112

**∴ The correct answer is ₹8112.**

**__Additional Information__**

Quarterly Compounding

When interest is **compounded quarterly**, the annual rate is divided by 4 and the time is multiplied by 4.

Effective Interest Rate

The **effective rate** for compounding can be calculated using the formula [ (1 + r/n)ⁿ − 1 ] × 100.

Compound Interest vs Simple Interest

For the **first period** (if compounding matches interest accrual), SI and CI are equal. Difference for 2 years is P(R/100)².
